circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometre motorsport venue located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke. Since 2009, it has been home to Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix and represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One track to open, following Bahrain's circuit.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing categories. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and renaming, the track returned to hosting the grand prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, measuring 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the sport in 2016 with the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix in the Middle East that same year, alongside hosting the Desert 400 for Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 until 2010 and various other racing categories. The FIA Grade 1 licensed track features multiple configurations and continues to host the annual Formula One race along with 24-hour endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian Grand Prix circuit at Spa-Francorchamps stretches 7. 004 kilometers through Wallonia near the town of Spa, establishing itself as a historic Formula One venue since its inaugural race in 1925. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix hosting from 1985 onward, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006, and featured prominently in motorsport's earliest era when it participated in the sport's inaugural championship season in 1950.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km street circuit that serves as the permanent home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its role in motorsport's premier series, the track has accommodated various other racing categories including international sports car championships, open-wheel series, and North American stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 through 2019 before resuming the event from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing competition, hosting the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit has served as the venue for Britain's Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating between three British tracks from 1955 to 1986, the championship race became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit near Budapest that hosted Formula One's historic 1986 Hungarian Grand Prix, marking the championship's first race in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park, with its inaugural race held as a tribute to Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Italy's Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, constructed in 1922 near Milan, spans 5. 793 kilometres and ranks among Europe's earliest purpose-built racing venues. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix almost annually since 1949, making it one of Formula One's most enduring venues, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" through its characteristic long straights and rapid corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility situated in Mie Prefecture and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The track regularly hosts major international racing events, most notably Formula One and Super Formula championships, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous boulevard lined with major hotels and casinos. The track incorporates iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix intermittently since 2015, following earlier stints on a different configuration that concluded in 1992, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that produces qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for the 2022 Formula One season, the venue has become the home of the Miami Grand Prix, with the track also adapted for electric racing events starting from 2025.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the harbour's perimeter in Monaco. Often called by its Monte Carlo name, the circuit is primarily situated within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to Formula One in 2021. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026, ending its run as a regular calendar fixture.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, Lusail International Circuit spans 5. 419 kilometres with a 1. 068-kilometre main straight and holds an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, this 4. 309 km circuit opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline, hosting the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in the Formula One calendar since its inaugural running in 2021. The track also accommodates international single-seater racing, including a newly added championship series beginning in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a temporary racing layout around the Marina Bay waterfront area.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner types, making it a comprehensive test of both speed and handling. With seating for 140,700 spectators and FIA Grade 1 certification, the venue hosts one of Europe's most prestigious motorsport events.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the venue for Formula One's United States Grand Prix alongside hosting major events in MotoGP, NASCAR, and sports car racing. The track has also accommodated various other motorsport series including IndyCar, rallycross, and international endurance championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British motorsport competitor who races for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the championship.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin and is a two-time Formula One World Champion, having claimed his titles in 2005 and 2006 during his tenure with Renault. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the F1 drivers' title and the World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes on the Formula One grid, having claimed eight race victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport competition.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as part of the Audi team, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has claimed two World Championship runner-up finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 race victories throughout his 13-season Formula One career. He currently competes for Cadillac in the championship.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for Alpine, bringing South American representation to the sport's premier series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his European endurance racing commitments with a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having made appearances at seven championship rounds between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One racing, competing for the Red Bull team. The driver holds both French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has established himself as one of the sport's most successful competitors, sharing the record of seven world championships with Michael Schumacher and holding numerous records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in endurance motorsport, capturing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW's factory team WRT, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, running from 2014 to 2020 and returning for 2022 through 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French driver currently racing for Haas in Formula One. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has yielded six race victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull before his recent move to the American team.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight race victories throughout his eight seasons in the championship.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following earlier stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen, competing for the Netherlands, drives for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. The Dutch and Belgian driver has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently working as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the championship from 2022 to 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated under the Alpine Racing banner from 2021 onwards, initially as Renault's factory squad before the manufacturer's withdrawal at season's end 2025. Previously competing as Renault F1 Team, the squad was rebranded to highlight Renault's Alpine sports car marque while maintaining its role as the French company's official racing entity.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin represents a British automotive manufacturer with a long history of Formula One participation under different organizational structures. The modern iteration, operated as AMR GP Limited, currently competes in the championship under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automobile maker, stands as Formula One's oldest continuously active team and its most accomplished outfit, having participated in every World Championship since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, famously nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after their emblem, remains a cornerstone of competitive motorsport history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, this squad entered the sport in 2016 and has been helmed since early 2024 by Ayao Komatsu, following the departure of the team's longstanding principal who had led it from its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established in 1970, this constructor gained prominence through endurance racing success including a 1989 Le Mans victory before joining Formula One in 1993. Operating as an independent team through numerous transformations, it became one of the longest-serving constructors in the championship's history until its 2025 departure, when Audi acquired its operations to establish their own factory effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited represents a prominent British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking, which operates as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group structure. The organization is currently under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a significant presence in Formula One since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier across different eras. The current works team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022. Mercedes-affiliated squads are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024, based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams in the sport, it operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in Formula One.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team to Red Bull Racing within the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a Formula One competitor since 2005 and remains one of two Grand Prix teams within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. Under Christian Horner's two-decade tenure as team principal until 2025, the outfit established itself as a major force in the sport, with the leadership subsequently transitioning to Laurent Mekies.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following Williams's earlier failed F1 venture, has operated from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters for decades. The team will compete as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026.
